exceptions.evidence: Where alcohol is permitted under ALC-01, it is capped at $30 per attendee: the USD total of the alcohol lines, divided by the attendee count. Spend above that cap is a medium exception.  Scope of ALC-01 and ALC-02. These two rules govern alcohol served on the premises — at restaurants, bars and hotels (MCC 5812, 5813 and 7011). Alcohol bought from any other merchant is retail and is governed by ALC-03 alone.
exceptions.explanation: $55.00 of alcohol per attendee against the $30.00 cap.

exceptions.evidence: Meal spend is capped at $75 per person per day for domestic travel and $100 per person per day for international travel. Spend above the cap is a medium exception. For this rule:  - a meal receipt is one declared as Meals - Individual, Meals - Team or Client Entertainment that contains food or drink — or, if it is not itemized, any receipt declared as one of those types; - meal spend is the USD total of the receipt's food, drink and gratuity lines (categories food_beverage, alcohol and service_fee) — anything else on the bill, such as a gift, is left out. For a receipt that is not itemized, it is the full receipt total; - per person means divided by the attendee count, or by one when no attendee count is recorded; - per day means the per-person amounts of all of one employee's meal receipts on the same calendar date, added together; - travel is international when the receipt's currency differs from the currency of the employee's home country, and domestic otherwise.  MEAL-01 applies to every meal receipt, whether or not it is part of a trip: "domestic" and "international" only choose which cap applies, and on a day that mixes the two, the higher cap applies. When a day's total is over the cap, raise MEAL-01 on every meal receipt that contributes to that day. For APAC and EMEA employees the regional cap in regional-addendum.md replaces both figures, and a breach is reported under REG-02 or REG-03 instead of MEAL-01.
exceptions.explanation: $214.80 per person on 2026-04-24 (receipts: RCP-015) against the $75.00 domestic daily cap.

exceptions.evidence: Gifts to clients and prospects are capped at **$50 per recipient per occasion**. An occasion is one receipt; lines on it that name the same recipient are added together for the cap, and the $10 test applies to each line. Spend above the cap is a medium exception. Any gift of $10 or more must also name its recipient, in the line description or elsewhere on the expense; an unnamed gift at that value is a medium exception. Cards and small tokens under $10 need no named recipient. Gift cards and other cash equivalents fall under GIFT-02 alone and are not also tested here. Unnamed gifts are each tested on their own, and when both parts of GIFT-01 apply, one exception cites every line involved.
exceptions.explanation: $180.00 for A. Moreau against the $50.00 per-recipient cap.
